title: /kb-item commits work before its claim is committed, so check-trailers refuses the push
goal: The kb-item skill commits the claimed item file on its own (a backlog-planning commit) right after backlog.py claim and before any work commit, so check-trailers, which reads the item as each commit has it, accepts the work commit; a test runs claim, a claim commit, a KB-Work work commit and check-trailers in a throwaway repository and passes, and fails with the claim commit left out.
notes: Failure it answers: in SP-liemltg2 a docs commit for TK-doyknj7i made after an uncommitted claim got the commit-msg warning "is todo, not claimed"; check-trailers would have refused its push, and the commit was redone with the claim committed first. /kb-item step 2 claims, step 6 commits the work, and the item file is committed only after done, so every /kb-item run hits this. /kb-sprint already commits claims before dispatch.
